subject: Clarify AcmeBio retention windows + audit-log exports (SIG/CAIQ follow-up)
thread_body:
From: Elena Sato <elena.sato@acmebio.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acmebio.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: AcmeBio: retention windows & audit-log export (SIG follow-up)

Hi Priya / Marcus,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. As part of our internal SIG review and CAIQ mapping, our security and privacy teams would like written confirmation on a few retention and export items before we move to the procurement step. High level asks:

- Confirm default retention windows for:
  * request/response payloads (customer prompts & model outputs)
   - operational/audit logs (routing, auth events, operator activity)
   - KV/prefix caches if those are persisted per-tenant
- Is there a standard contract amendment you offer to extend retention for audit logs (we may need 12 months for our audit trail)?
- Can you produce a sample (sanitized) audit-log export in CSV with the fields we saw in the demo?
- During our SOC 2 review can Redwood place a temporary legal hold while we validate? If so, what is the process and lead time?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with specific CAIQ/SIG question IDs we need to close. Can you confirm who we should engage for the evidence and an expected timeline (we're targeting completion before our Q2 vendor board).

Cheers,
Elena Sato
Head of InfoSec, AcmeBio
[attachment: Acme_SIG_questions.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Elena Sato <elena.sato@acmebio.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeBio: retention windows & audit-log export (SIG follow-up)

Elena — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR: we can provide the exports and options you're asking about; some longer tails (12+ months) require contract addenda for hosted customers or Dedicated capacity. Proposed next steps below.

Short answers up front (we'll follow with attachments and a sample):
- Default retention: request/response payloads 30 days; operational/audit logs 90 days; cache artifacts (KV/prefix) are ephemeral by default (30 days) unless configured by the customer.
- Extension: we offer audit-log retention extensions up to 24 months for enterprise customers via an amendment (add-on fee, SLA change). For Hosted customers there are data residency and KMS constraints we need to confirm.
- Audit-log sample: Soojin will attach a sanitized CSV with the schema we export.
- Legal hold: we support temporary preservation requests; the standard process is a written request to security@redwood.ai + signed amendment for holds >30 days. Lead time: 2 business days to confirm, 5 business days to fully enact exports/preservation for Hosted accounts.

I'll coordinate internally — Marcus will outline exact field names and TTL knobs; Soojin will produce the CSV. Can you confirm if AcmeBio needs payloads (prompts & outputs) preserved beyond 30 days, or if audit logs alone suffice for the SIG evidence? Also flag any regulatory constraints (EU/Schengen residency) if the sample needs to be region-specific.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
[internal note: loop in legal for amendment language once scope confirmed]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Sato <elena.sato@acmebio.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 12:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeBio: retention windows & audit-log export (SIG follow-up)

Elena / team — adding a quick technical summary so expectations are clear. This is the data model we typically reference in responses and the SIG/CAIQ mapping: 

1) Request/response payloads (customer prompts & model outputs)
   - Default retention: 30 days for Hosted API.
   - For Dedicated customers we can configure to N days; persistent storage is customer-scoped and can be extended via policy.

2) Operational & audit logs (auth events, routing, operator actions)
   - Default retention: 90 days.
   - Exportable schema includes: timestamp (UTC), tenant_id, event_type, actor_id, request_id, resource, result_code, user_agent, region, retention_flag. See attached sample (audit-log-sample.csv).

3) KV/prefix caches
   - Not persisted to durable storage for Hosted by default; eviction TTL ~30d. For Dedicated we offer optional checkpointing with explicit consent.

4) Legal hold / preservation
   - We can place a preservation hold on a tenant's records for up to 90 days without a signed amendment (operational freeze). For holds >90 days we require an addendum that covers storage costs and any applicable KMS key management changes.

5) Data residency & encryption
   - Exports can be delivered from region-specific clusters if you are using EU-hosted endpoints. Keys remain customer-specific for Dedicated via KMS; Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS unless otherwise arranged.

Soojin — attaching the sanitized CSV now for Elena's team. Priya — once Elena confirms fields and retention target, I can draft the contract language for the amendment.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference
[attachment: audit-log-sample.csv (csv)]

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we run these through our SIG reviewers: 

- For our SOC 2 scope we need 12 months of audit logs retained and a statement that preservation can be started immediately upon request. The 90-day default is fine, but can Redwood commit to immediate preservation (no deletion) while we finalize the amendment? If so, please document the ask procedure and point person.
- The CSV looks good; can you include an additional column for "hash_of_payload" (or a deterministic fingerprint) so our auditors can verify tamper-evidence without receiving actual payloads?
- We will need a CAIQ redline for questions related to logging and retention. I've attached a preliminary redline doc.

If you can confirm the hold process and timeline (and provide a DocuSign amendment for 12 months), we'll schedule a short 30-minute sync with our procurement team for next Wednesday.

Elena
